title: Two Lists of Stones: De lapidibus and the Apocalypse — a groundwork note on relations, withholding readings (v0.1)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: Two short Greek books three centuries apart catalogue the same stones in nearly the same words, use the same word for a seal, and name the same crimson with the same grain. This note establishes the relations and withholds the readings, in the register of Catalogues and Wills (#1581). Recorded: the overlap of the stone-lists item by item, with Theophrastus ordering by δύναμις (what a stone can do — colours water like the emerald, petrifies, draws, tests gold like the Lydian stone) and John ordering by position (first to twelfth foundation, Rev 21:19–20); the two senses of σφραγίς — the seal carved FROM the red unburnable ἄνθραξ at Miletus, ἐν ᾧπερ καὶ τὰ ἑξάγωνα, against the seal set UPON the book of Rev 5:1, upon persons at 7:3–4 (and then counted), and upon speech as a prohibition against writing at 10:4 — together with the closing counter-instruction μὴ σφραγίσῃς (22:10) and the curse of 22:18 as the seal's replacement technology; κόκκινον as one word at two ends of a supply chain, the pigment ground and settled above Ephesus (ἐν ᾧπέρ ἐστι τὸ τῆς τέχνης; τὸ μὲν ὑφιστάμενον κάτω κιννάβαρι, τὸ δ᾽ ἐπάνω καὶ πλεῖον πλύσμα) and dated to a named inventor ninety years back, against the same word worn by the woman and the beast and freighted in the merchants' manifest at 18:12; the hexagons in the mineral against the tetragon of the measured cube; and the white ψῆφος of Rev 2:17 bearing a name known only to its receiver, set against stones whose knowledge is public because the test repeats — an instrument, or an address. No dependence asserted, no source proposed, no allegory offered; Exodus 28 and Ezekiel 28 named as John's older relatives and untraced, because tracing them is the reading. Extracted from the notebook The First Draft §34 and §34.1.

wiki_article: "Two Lists of Stones" is a groundwork note by Lee Sharks (7 September 2026) setting the relations between Theophrastus's De lapidibus and the Apocalypse of John and withholding the readings. The two books catalogue the same stones — emerald, sard, sardonyx, amethyst, hyacinth, crystal — in nearly the same words, but Theophrastus orders them by what each can do (colour water, petrify, draw, test gold like the Lydian stone) and John by where each stands (first to twelfth foundation of the city wall). The note records the two senses of σφραγίς: in Theophrastus the seal is carved FROM the red unburnable ἄνθραξ at Miletus, in which also are the hexagons; in John it is set UPON a book, upon persons who are then counted, and upon speech as a prohibition against writing — against the closing instruction not to seal this book at all. It records κόκκινον as one word at two ends of a supply chain: the pigment ground, washed and settled above Ephesus, credited to a named inventor ninety years back, and the same crimson worn by the woman and the beast and freighted in the merchants' manifest. It sets the hexagons in the mineral beside the tetragon of the measured cube, and the white ψῆφος bearing a name known only to its receiver beside stones whose knowledge is public because the test repeats — an instrument, or an address. No dependence is asserted and no allegory offered; Exodus 28 and Ezekiel 28 are named as John's older relatives and left untraced, because tracing them is the reading. Extracted from the notebook The First Draft (§34, §34.1).

defines_concepts.definition: The two constructions of a stone's legibility set side by side in this note: a stone known by a repeatable public test (Theophrastus's Lydian stone, the unburnable ἄνθραξ) against a stone whose whole content is a name legible only to its receiver (Revelation's white ψῆφος).
